newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends lower on bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends lower on bearish sentiment.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended lower for the fifth straight session Friday as bearish sentiment tightened its hold on the oil market which was still shaken by steep losses Thursday.
"People are still a bit shell-shocked, and nobody seems to want to buy crude with this new bearish market," said Al Lindseth, a trader with GSC Energy.

December crude ended off 32 cents at $23.03 a barrel. Crude's losses weighed on refined products. December heating oil settled off 0.25 cent at 66.60 cents a gallon while Dec gasoline ended up a mere 0.09 cent at 64.70 cents a gallon.
"Gasoline fundamentals are good given the inventory situation and refinery turnarounds," said Smith Barney analyst John Saucer.

Gasoline stocks are at historical lows, but refineries are undergoing seasonal maintenance and maximizing distillate output ahead of winter, so gasoline stocks are not seen rebuilding significantly in the short term.

Crude was unable to strengthen when the U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations said Friday that Iraq was making "outrageous demands" on how a deal to partially lift a bar on oil exports should be implemented.
Ambassador Madeleine Albright made the statment after the U.N. Security Council voted at its regular 60-day review to hold in place broad sanctions against Iraq.
"As an example of the bearish sentiment, we got no response out of Madeleine Albright growling at Iraq," said Tim Evans, an analyst at Pegasus Econometric Group.
Disagreement between the United States and Iraq continues to put on ice a deal which would allow Iraq tosell $2 billion worth of oil in exchange for food.
Meanwhile, chartists said crude's close near $23.00 made it technically weak, as it was left poised to test $22.85, the start of a price gap on a spot month continuation chart that extends to $22.25.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
